definitions.explanation: To firmly establish something significant, such as a policy, record, or system. Carries a sense of creating something lasting and important. Commonly used for setting records in sports or establishing diplomatic relations.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}{記録|きろく}を{樹立|じゅりつ}した。
{両国|りょうこく}は{外交|がいこう}{関係|かんけい}を{樹立|じゅりつ}した。
examples.english: The two countries established diplomatic relations.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はオリンピックで{新記録|しんきろく}を{樹立|じゅりつ}し、{金|きん}メダルを{獲得|かくとく}した。
examples.english: She set a new record at the Olympics and won a gold medal.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal suru verb ({樹立|じゅりつ}する). Most commonly used for setting records ({記録|きろく}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する) or establishing formal relations or systems. The kanji {樹|じゅ} (tree) conveys the metaphor of planting something that will stand firm.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記録|きろく}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する: to set a record
- {世界|せかい}{記録|きろく}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する: to set a world record
- {外交|がいこう}{関係|かんけい}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する: to establish diplomatic relations
- {政権|せいけん}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する: to establish a government
